consensus_summary: The highway primarily symbolizes the prepared way of the Lord / Highway of Holiness: God’s route of salvation and deliverance by which He comes to His people and the redeemed return, open to the holy and closed to the unclean (anchored in Isa 35:8 and 40:3 with NT application to John the Baptist).
book_summary: The Way of holiness—the prepared road home, made straight and smooth, where the wicked do not walk.
consensus_core_identification: prepared Highway of Holiness / way of the Lord for salvation, God’s coming, and the redeemed’s return
book_core_identification: Way of holiness: prepared straight smooth road home closed to the wicked
rationale: Both reduce to the identical Isaianic core (esp. 35:8 and 40:3–4) of the prepared holy highway for the Lord’s coming and the redeemed’s safe return home; wording differences (“road home,” “straight and smooth,” “wicked do not walk”) are immaterial restatements of the same referent and boundaries already present in the consensus primary meaning and its dominant bases. No replacement of referent, no material narrowing or broadening of cases, and no contradiction.
strongest_objection: The book’s brief phrasing omits explicit NT/John-the-Baptist or Gentile-inclusion layers that some consensus responses list as common, yet these are extensions of the same core rather than competing identifications, so they do not disturb equivalence.
